answer.decision: Adopt a managed search service with portability safeguards.
answer.action: Launch within four months using the managed service behind an internal search abstraction. Generate vendor-neutral canonical search documents, maintain a portable indexing pipeline, and regularly test bulk export and reindexing into an alternative engine.
reasons: The managed service already provides faceting, typo tolerance, and near-real-time indexing, while the internal prototype still lacked key features after six engineer-weeks.
Building and operating an open-source cluster conflicts with the backend team's capacity and the prohibition on increasing operational on-call headcount.
Delaying for dedicated hires would miss the four-month deadline and risks forfeiting the contracted design-partner expansion.
The projected year-one cost is modest at 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
A canonical document model, internal abstraction, and documented bulk export API provide a practical migration path and reduce vendor lock-in.
assumptions: The managed service can satisfy the required reliability, security, privacy, and compliance standards.
Its pricing remains acceptable under plausible traffic growth beyond year one.
The internal abstraction covers application-facing query and indexing contracts without attempting to normalize every vendor-specific feature.
The bulk export API includes sufficient document and configuration data, or missing relevance configuration can be versioned internally.
risks: Vendor-specific relevance behavior or query features may leak through the abstraction and increase later migration effort.
Costs may rise materially as traffic, index size, or query complexity grows.
Export capability alone does not guarantee a fast migration; reindexing performance and relevance parity could become bottlenecks.
Service outages, quotas, regional availability, or roadmap changes remain external dependencies.
Overengineering the portability layer could threaten the four-month launch schedule.

citations.claim: The internal prototype required six engineer-weeks but delivered only basic keyword search without typo tolerance or faceting.
The managed service supports all launch requirements and provides a documented bulk export API.
Projected year-one managed-service spend is 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
Operating an open-source cluster requires a rotating primary on-call owner and quarterly upgrades.
A six-month delay would forgo a contracted design-partner expansion.
The product can produce vendor-neutral canonical search documents before indexing.
